questions.prompt: By default, what does OpenAI's MCP tool do before data goes to a remote server?

options.text: It asks for your approval first, so you can review what is shared
options.explanation: Right. The OpenAI docs say OpenAI requests your approval before any data is shared with a connector or remote MCP server.

options.text: It shares everything at once and only tells you after the call
options.explanation: The default is the other way round. It asks first.

options.text: It blocks every remote server until a studio admin turns on a setting for it
options.explanation: The page describes no such block. It describes approvals.

questions.prompt: For a read-only assistant, what do the Claude docs recommend for write or destructive MCP tools?

options.text: Leave them on, since the model will not use a write tool unless it is asked to
options.explanation: The model can call any tool that is on. The Claude docs recommend turning write tools off.

options.text: Denylist them, so that the model cannot call them in a read-only assistant
options.explanation: Right. The Claude docs recommend denylisting write or destructive tools when building read-only assistants.

options.text: Rename them so that they sound harmless to anyone who reads the tool list
options.explanation: A new name changes nothing about what the tool can do.

questions.prompt: Why do the OpenAI docs warn about URLs that come from tool outputs?

options.text: They can be dangerous to use unless you trust the service that gave them
options.explanation: Right. The OpenAI docs say it can be dangerous to request URLs or embed image URLs from tool outputs.

options.text: They are always slower than links typed by a person, so pages load late for users
options.explanation: The warning is about safety, not speed.

options.text: They cost extra tokens every time they are shown to the model at all
options.explanation: The warning is about trust, not cost.
